title: Derived tensor product of perfect objects is perfect
statement: Let (X,\mathcal O_X) be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let K,L be perfect objects [def-pc-perfect-complex] of D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. Then the derived tensor product K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}L is a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_X).

proof.text: At each x, apply lem-pc-perfect-common-affine-models to K and L. It gives one affine neighbourhood U of x and strictly perfect complexes A,B, together with representing isomorphisms for the two restricted objects. This implements the common-refinement step without duplicating the restriction argument.

Prove strictlyPerfect_totalTensor directly in Lean. If A is supported in [a,b] and B in [c,d], the tensor total term vanishes outside [a+c,b+d]: each summand has a zero factor. In degree n, use the finite index set J={(p,q):p+q=n and a<=p<=b}. Tensor the two finite-free retract pairs. The freeTensorFreeIso identifies their target with the free sheaf on the product of the two finite bases. Assemble these retracts by biproduct.map. The total term retracts onto the sum over J, by mapBifunctorDesc and its summand equations; all omitted summands are zero. The sum of the free targets is free on the dependent sum of the finite bases, reindexed by ULift(Fin(card)). The composite retraction is the identity, proving strict perfectness.

Map eP and eN under exact restriction and compose with the local representing isomorphisms. Apply lem-sc-strict-perfect-tensor-local-comparison with these prescribed local models. Its comparison identifies the restriction of Q(Tot(P tensor N)) with Q(Tot(A tensor B)). Combine this comparison with the strict perfectness proved in step 2 and the membership x in U. The definition def-pc-perfect-complex then gives perfectness at every point.
